evidence.claim: Edge of the Wilderness follows Highway 38 for 47 miles between Effie and Grand Rapids, through pine and hardwood forest, lakes and rolling hills.
evidence.quote: Length 47 miles Route Hwy. 38 between Grand Rapids and Effie. Scenery Pine and hardwood forest, lakes, rolling hills.

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration identifies this winding road as a National Scenic Byway and recommends three hours to visit its length.
evidence.quote: National Scenic Byway • Minnesota Length 47 mi / 75.6 km Time to Allow Three hours to visit the entire byway

evidence.claim: Its description singles out lakes, swamps and the fall colors of sugar maple, oak, aspen and birch.
evidence.quote: During fall, the northwoods is adorned with the brilliant colors of red sugar maples, bronze oak trees and glowing gold aspen and birch.

State Highway 38 was authorized in 1933.

evidence.quote: The site of the town center was originally at a store operated by John Lundeen on Big Turtle Lake, but was moved in 1910 to its present location near the railway.

evidence.claim: Marcell’s town center moved to meet the railway.
evidence.quote: The site of the town center was originally at a store operated by John Lundeen on Big Turtle Lake, but was moved in 1910 to its present location near the railway.

evidence.claim: Founded as Turtle Lake in 1905, the community changed its name the following year because other places already used it.
evidence.quote: Marcell was founded under the name Turtle Lake in 1905.  The name was changed to Marcell the following year due to a name conflict with other communities named Turtle Lake.

evidence.claim: The new name honored Andy Marcell, a Minneapolis and Rainy River Railway conductor involved in a local railway accident.
evidence.quote: The name Marcell is in honor of Andy Marcell, a conductor on the former Minneapolis and Rainy River Railway, who was involved in a railway accident in the area.

evidence.claim: In 1910, the center shifted from John Lundeen’s store on Big Turtle Lake to its present location near the tracks.
evidence.quote: The site of the town center was originally at a store operated by John Lundeen on Big Turtle Lake, but was moved in 1910 to its present location near the railway.

evidence.claim: Marcell lies within the Chippewa National Forest, 28 miles north of Grand Rapids.
evidence.quote: Marcell is located 28 miles north of Grand Rapids.  The community is located within the Chippewa National Forest.

evidence.claim: Highways 38 and 286 are now two of the community’s main routes.
evidence.quote: Minnesota State Highways 38 and 286 are two of the main routes in the community.

evidence.claim: A reconstructed logging camp and an original fire tower tell different parts of the forest story at Grand Rapids’s Forest History Center.
evidence.quote: a living history lumber camp, an original 1934 fire tower, and nature trails.

evidence.claim: The camp re-creates 1900, with a bunkhouse, cook house, blacksmith shop and horse barn.
evidence.quote: The Logging Camp is a re-creation of a typical logging camp of 1900. Buildings include a bunkhouse, cook house, blacksmith shop, horse barn, and outhouse.

evidence.claim: The 100-foot tower was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1934 and moved here.
evidence.quote: Forest Lookout Tower is an original structure built in 1934 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, and moved on location. It is 100 feet high

evidence.claim: The forest service cabin and tool shed are reproductions of buildings used by patrolmen and firefighting crews in the 1930s.
evidence.quote: The forest service cabin and tool shed are reproductions of what were used to house patrolmen and by fire fighting crews during the 1930s.

evidence.claim: Beside the Mississippi, a replica floating cook shack and bunkhouse recalls the river drivers who moved logs downstream to mills.
evidence.quote: The river wanigan is a 1901 replica of a floating cook shack and bunkhouse once used by river drivers when moving logs down river to the mills.

evidence.claim: Beside the Mississippi
evidence.quote: on wooded acreage adjoining the Mississippi River
